# lnurlcash-core (Rust)

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer notes: the money-critical logic, with UniFFI bindings
for Kotlin and Swift. MIT.

cargo add lnurlcash-core

## Layout

protocol   pure: builds Requests, parses responses. No I/O. Always available.
client     optional feature "client": a thin reqwest loop over protocol.
ffi        optional feature "ffi": UniFFI export of the PURE half only.

The Request/parse split is the point: a caller with its own HTTP stack uses
protocol directly, and nothing async crosses the FFI boundary.

## Core API

protocol::note_info_request(url) -> Request { url, new_secrets, outputs }
protocol::parse_note_info(&Value, queried_url, Policy) -> WithdrawRequestInfo
protocol::rotate_request(callback, k1, new_secret) -> Request
protocol::split_request(callback, k1s, amount_msat, new_secret, change_secret) -> Request
protocol::merge_request(callback, k1s, new_secret) -> Request
protocol::melt_request(callback, k1, bolt11) -> Request
protocol::parse_mutation(&Value, MutationKind, &request.outputs, Policy)
  -> MutationResponse. outputs = what the rotate/split/merge named, recorded
  on the Request: [output], or [output, change] for a split. A cp1 output is
  owed its cs1 in sig (sig2 for a split's change) ALWAYS, whatever the
  policy; without it the mutation is Unverifiable. A plain hash output is
  unsigned by design (LUD-25 Part 2 certifies cp1 notes only): signature
  None, no error. A missing output reads as a hash. MutationKind::{Melt,
  Rotate,Split,Merge} - a melt mints nothing and owes none.
protocol::Policy { require_signatures, require_mint_pubkey }  defaults false
  and true. require_signatures also demands the old Part 1 sig over a hash
  output. require_mint_pubkey refuses a withdrawRequest with no valid
  mintPubkey; off only for a Part 1-only mint. Build with ..Policy::default().
protocol::pay_request_request / invoice_request / verify_request + parse_*

verify_note_signature(k1, amount_msat, sig_hex_or_cs1, mint_pubkey_hex) -> bool
generate_note_secret() -> String    hash_k1(k1) -> Result<String>

cash::derive_cash_root(seed) -> CashNode        LUD-25's scheme, BIP-32 m/139'
cash::derive_cash_domain_node(root, host)       m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, d1..d4 =
  HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, host)[0..16] as 4 RAW big-endian uint32.
  RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the levels are, decided by
  the host name. NEVER mask the top bit, NEVER harden all four - either
  derives a different tree and restores nothing, silently.
cash::derive_cash_secret(root, host, i) / cash::cash_secret_at(node, i)
  below the domain node there is no unhardened level, so a signer given the
  node needs no curve - that is why the node is its own step
cash::cash_node_to_hex / from_hex     privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
cash::derive_cash_child(node, raw_u32)          BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking
  this crate against BIP-32's own vectors
cash::derive_cash_master(seed) -> CashNode      the BIP-32 master, for walking
  a path this crate does not name
cash::CashSecretSource::{new, next_secret, next_index}
secrets::derive_note_root / derive_note_secret  LEGACY pre-spec HMAC scheme.
  Do not mint under it; still scanned so old notes stay findable.
note::build_note_info_url_by_hash(withdraw_link, h) -> Option<String>
  the ?h= informational GET, so a restore walk keeps secrets off the wire.
  A rejection proves nothing: unsupported, unknown and BURNED are one answer.
  The persisted per-host counter is the real backup, not the scan.
  h may be a Part 2 cp1, sent as p.

LUD-25 Part 2 (recoverable::): a note keyed by a public key, spent by a
recoverable signature
encode_cp1/decode_cp1/is_cp1   note pubkey, 32-byte x-only, bech32m "cp"
encode_ck1/decode_ck1/is_ck1   bearer secret, 65-byte r||s||recid, "ck"
encode_cs1/decode_cs1/is_cs1   mint certificate over hex(pk), same layout, "cs"
encode_cx1/decode_cx1/is_cx1   watch-only branch Cx1 { pubkey_x_only,
  chain_code }, "cx". Decoders return None, never panic. No length limit;
  all-uppercase accepted; mixed case, a bech32 (not bech32m) checksum, the
  wrong hrp or length and non-zero padding refused (BIP-350)
derive_cash_address_node(root, host) -> CashNode   m/139'/1'/d1..d4, hashing
  key m/139'/1'/0. The REFERENCE WALLET's path, not the spec text's
  m/139'/d1..d4 (that is the Part 1 ladder's node, and finds none of its notes)
cash_node_to_cx1(node) -> Cx1
derive_note_pubkey(P, chain_code, i) -> pk     watch-only, BIP-341 style
  tweak; i any u32, 4-byte big-endian, never hardened. t >= n is an error,
  never reduced: use the next index
derive_note_secret_key(p, chain_code, i) -> sk   negates p first when P has
  odd y
sign_note_ownership(sk) -> [u8; 65]   RFC6979, low-S, over the fixed
  "LNURLcash"; note_ownership_digest() is the digest
recover_note_ownership_pubkey(sig) -> Option<pk>
note_id_of(k1) -> Option<id>   sha256(k1) for a secret, the recovered key for
  a ck1. One note has many valid ck1 strings: compare notes by this, not k1
note_lookup_of(k1) -> Option<String>   the hash, or the cp1 for a ck1
verify_note_signature also takes a ck1 as k1 and a cs1 as the signature;
  verify_note_signature_hash(id, ..) checks a certificate by pk or hash
Wire: a ck1 goes wherever a k1 does; a cp1 wherever an output does.
  mint_invoice_request_with_hash: the comment alone (a hash also sends h).
  rotate/split/merge_request_with_hash: p1/p2 for a cp1, h/h2 for a hash
  parse_note_info compares the echoed k1 as the note it names (by note id),
  as all the kits do: a mint echoing the high-S twin of our ck1 is the same
  note; another key is still refused
derive_nostr_cash_seed(sk) / derive_nostr_address_node(sk, host)   NOT
  LUD-25: a branch from a Nostr identity key, via
  HMAC-SHA256(key = sk, msg = "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"), then the address path
resolve_note_input / resolve_mint_input / resolve_lnurl_input
parse_mint_fee / apply_mint_fee / gross_up_for_mint_fee
build_note_url / with_new_k1 / without_k1
decode_bolt11_amount_msat / is_bolt11_invoice / same_invoice

client::Client::{fetch_note_info, rotate_note, split_note, merge_notes,
melt_note, settle_note, probe_burned_note, fetch_pay_request, request_invoice,
fetch_invoice_verification, fetch_mint_address}

## Errors

Error::RequestRefused   nothing sent, note untouched
Error::ServiceRejected  processed and refused (definitive)
Error::NotePending      a melt is in flight on this k1 - retry, NOT spent
Error::NoteSpent { reason, new_secrets }    authoritative at the info GET.
  From a MUTATION at a service that will not replay a retry, it is also what
  an ALREADY-APPLIED mutation looks like - read new_secrets before believing
Error::NoteUnknown { reason, new_secrets }  service does not recognise it
Error::Ambiguous { message, new_secrets }   outcome UNKNOWN
Error::Unverifiable { message, new_secrets }  the mutation LANDED and a cp1
  output came back with no cs1 (or a hash output unsigned under
  require_signatures). The note is REAL - persist new_secrets (empty from a
  *_with_hash call: the caller holds that key), then report the mint
Error::Protocol         a non-mutating response did not match the spec,
  which includes a withdrawRequest publishing no mintPubkey (unless
  require_mint_pubkey is off)

err.is_ambiguous() and err.is_definitive() are the two questions worth asking.
err.new_secrets() carries the secrets out of any error that could describe a
mutation the service applied - ambiguous, unverifiable, spent or unknown.
PERSIST them before anything else, then probe_burned_note.

client::ClientConfig { policy, mutation_retries, .. }
  mutation_retries defaults to 1. LUD-25 requires a service to answer a
  byte-identical retried rotate/split/merge with the original success, so a
  lost answer is re-asked rather than given up on. NEVER a melt: it carries
  pr, is paid asynchronously and has no replay guarantee. The request is
  re-sent byte for byte - the replay is matched on the k1 set, h, h2 and
  amount, so a fresh secret would make it a different mutation.

## Rules

1. max_withdrawable is the ONLY authoritative value. A note URL's `amount` is a claim.
2. The WALLET generates replacement secrets; disclose only sha256(secret).
   Never accept a service-supplied k1.
3. Ambiguous means MAYBE. Save new_secrets, then probe.
4. A melt's OK means IN FLIGHT.
5. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note.
6. Never log note URLs - the secret is in the query string.
7. Amounts are integer milli-satoshis, u64, everywhere.

## Porting hazards (both in the vectors)

- floor(gross*ppm/1e6) overflows u64 at realistic amounts. Compute split:
  (g/1e6)*ppm + ((g%1e6)*ppm)/1e6
- gross-up must be binary search; estimate-then-walk is unbounded near 100% fee.

## Bindings

cargo run --features bindgen --bin uniffi-bindgen -- generate \
  --library target/release/liblnurlcash_core.dylib --language kotlin --out-dir bindings

FfiRequest { url, new_secrets, outputs }
FfiPolicy { require_signatures = false, require_mint_pubkey = true }
parse_note_info(body, queried_url, FfiPolicy) -> FfiWithdrawInfo
parse_mutation(body, new_secrets, kind, outputs, FfiPolicy) -> FfiMutation
  pass request.newSecrets AND request.outputs back: without outputs a cp1
  output is read as a hash and its missing certificate goes unnoticed
